No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Kogi Govt Probes Nursing Student’s Death Amid Protest Over Alleged Negligence by Ibrahim Obansa 5 seconds ago in Health , North Central Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The Kogi State Government has ordered an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of a 20-year-old nursing student, Adewumi Olamide Gift, following protests by students of the Kogi State College of Nursing Sciences, Obangede, Okehi Local Government Area.
Olamide, a 300-level student of the institution, reportedly died after falling ill on November 9, 2026, the day her semester examinations commenced, amid allegations of negligence by the college management and inadequate medical facilities.
Students alleged that the deceased collapsed in the examination hall but was taken to the school’s sick bay, where she was reportedly still expected to sit for the examination.
The deceased’s parents, who reportedly travelled from Lagos following the development, took her first to the Confluence University of Science and Technology (CUSTECH) Teaching Hospital, Okene, before transferring her to the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Lokoja, where she eventually died.
The incident sparked protests on Monday as students shut the institution’s main gate, accusing the management of gross negligence and demanding accountability over the circumstances surrounding their colleague’s death.
Reacting to the incident, the Kogi State Government expressed condolences to the family of the deceased, describing her death as painful, while assuring students and the public that the circumstances surrounding the tragedy would be thoroughly investigated.
Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, directed the Commissioner for Health, Dr Abdulazeez Adams Adeiza, to immediately investigate the incident, adding that a team had been deployed to the college to conduct a comprehensive probe.
In a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Communications, Kingsley Femi Fanwo, the government assured the bereaved family, students and members of the public that the investigation would be thorough and transparent.
The government also extended condolences to the family, management, staff and students of the college, praying for strength for the bereaved family and the repose of the soul of the deceased.
